figures.caption: Synthetic transport domain with a clean-water inlet, zero-gradient outlet and reflecting lateral walls. Shading identifies initial-pulse support, not uniform density. Both upstream diffusive export and downstream advective export enter the mass budget.
Output-grid cell faces in physical coordinates. The plotted grid is 200 × 23; training labels use 400 × 48 and the accuracy reference uses 800 × 92 cells.

Implemented training and verification workflow. Numerical labels and the finer evaluation reference have different resolutions. Frozen hydraulic-interpolation tests are separate from supported training configurations; no field-validation dataset is used.

Six dimensionless physical inputs are mapped to seven features and passed through three 64-unit Tanh hidden layers. A Softplus output and analytical coordinate/inlet transforms enforce nonnegativity and boundary conditions; initial, PDE and mass constraints remain soft.

Recorded hybrid optimization objectives for seed 2026. Adam and L-BFGS use different sampling/objective details and are plotted separately. Closure evaluations include line-search trials and are not optimizer iterations; no monotone convergence is implied.

Finite-volume control cell and oriented face fluxes. Interior flux contributions cancel between adjacent cells. Advection uses an upwind face value and diffusion uses a central face gradient. Diagram is schematic, not a physical grid.

Finite-volume errors against the independent analytical advection–diffusion eigenmode. The dashed line indicates first-order scaling anchored at the coarsest result; the finest reference is not compared with itself.
Time-resolved MSE and RMSE against the 800 × 92 reference restricted to output cells. Synthetic plain/normal configuration; seed 2026; 200 × 23 output cells; T=300 s.
Signed hybrid prediction minus restricted FVM reference at t=300 s. Synthetic plain/normal configuration; seed 2026; 200 × 23 output cells; T=300 s.

Flux-inclusive budget residual, normalized by each method’s prescribed-grid initial mass. Neural flux is integrated by the recorded output-time trapezoidal diagnostic; FVM export is integrated during internal steps. Neural maximum absolute budget error is 0.4483%.

Unweighted Adam component losses and held-out label MSE for hybrid seed 2026. Validation labels are a split of the numerical label pool, not field observations or the finer evaluation reference. Boundary loss is omitted from the plot because its architectural enforcement keeps it near roundoff.

Prescribed widths of the four synthetic terrain configurations. All reaches have length 1000 m. This replaces the old geographic-location map; no geographic calibration or surveyed site geometry is implied.

Prescribed compact initial pulse sampled at output-cell centres. It is independent of the neural prediction and common to both formulations. Initial support is 100<x<400 m, with transverse modulation; density is in kg/m².
Hybrid PINN field at 300 s. Identical axes and colour limits are used in Figs. 14 and 15. Synthetic plain/normal configuration; seed 2026; 200 × 23 output cells; T=300 s.
FVM reference field at 300 s. Identical axes and colour limits are used in Figs. 14 and 15. Synthetic plain/normal configuration; seed 2026; 200 × 23 output cells; T=300 s.

Per-time relative L2 error of the baseline hybrid prediction. The final-time value is 2.1648%; the joint space–time relative L2 is 1.2318% and is a different statistic. This replaces the duplicated MSE figure.
Baseline signed errors at 100, 200 and 300 s, with shared symmetric colour limits. Seed 2026; all axes are physical coordinates.

Remaining mass and cumulative outward boundary export for the baseline. Decreasing in-domain mass is expected as the pulse exits. Conservation is assessed through their sum and the initial mass, as in Fig. 10.

Measured CPU rollout time for equal 200 × 23 × 61 output workloads. AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX; two PyTorch threads; ten repetitions after one warm-up, alternating order. Training and loading are excluded. Neural inference is approximately 6.33 times slower.

Baseline final fields at 300 s for the FVM reference, hybrid and data-only models, using shared colour limits and seed 2026. Both neural models share positivity/boundary architecture; hybrid training additionally uses physical and integrated-mass information. Three-seed statistics are reported in Table X.
Mountain/wet prediction at 100 s. Seed 2026; width 52.8 m. This snapshot is explicitly at 100 s, while reported scenario metrics cover the complete 0–300 s trajectory.
Mountain/wet signed error at 100 s. Seed 2026; width 52.8 m. This snapshot is explicitly at 100 s, while reported scenario metrics cover the complete 0–300 s trajectory.

Pointwise 90th-percentile absolute residual from the first 30 output times (0–145 s). Half-widths define descriptive numerical residual intervals, not guaranteed conformal intervals or field uncertainty. Evaluation on the remaining 31 times yields 72.5989% coverage.

Empirical coverage on output times 150–300 s using half-widths estimated on 0–145 s. The diagonal is nominal equality, not a fitted calibration curve. Temporal dependence prevents claiming an exchangeability-based coverage guarantee.

All ten recorded baseline CPU timing repetitions under the protocol of Fig. 19. Execution order alternates; these are the original recorded timings, not new measurements. This is Fig. 25 in the revised document and replaces Fig. 26 in the original.
